Q: How does vertical text work for table cells in the paged media module? A:

You're using 2 commands that both affect the text direction:

transform: rotate(-180); this rotates the text.

writing-mode: vertical-rl; which sets a writing mode (characters below each other), this is used for e.g. Japanese. Your character spacing will be a side effect of this.

EDIT: I previously recommended using transform: rotate(90deg); but that has a major flaw: the text is rotated, but the box that contains the text still has the original dimensions. In the question, we see table cells that are tall and narrow. When you transform that cell, it is still tall and narrow, so the text ends up outside the cell, AND the text is wrapped instead of fitting on one line.

Using writing-mode is the only way to correct this without resorting to magic numbers that only work for one size of cell.

In Antennahouse Formatter 7.3, writing-mode works correctly.

To place text vertically, rotated 90° to the right (so it reads top to bottom):

writing-mode: vertical-rl;

To place text vertically, rotated 90° to the left (so it reads bottom to top), you do have to add a rotation because writing-mode does not have any options for orienting text bottom to top.

    writing-mode: vertical-rl;
    transform: rotate(180deg);

In both cases the spacing looks correct for English and other Latin languages.
